problem: A writer is editing the first draft of a book. On average, each sentence has a $5%$ chance of containing a typo. What is the probability of finding the first typo in the $4$th sentence or later? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Probability of a Geometric Random Variable on an Unbounded Interval
examples.problem: A company is conducting interviews to fill a job. On average, $35\%$ of applicants meet all the requirements. What is the probability that an applicant who meets all the requirements will appear for the first time after the $3$rd interviewee? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
examples.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x) = (1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of applicants interviewed until an applicant who meets all requirements appears. Since the chance of finding an applicant who meets all the requirements is $35\%,$ the number of applicants interviewed until an applicant who meets all requirements appears can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success

$$
p = 35\% = \dfrac{35}{100} = 0.35.
$$

So, $X\sim\textrm{Geom}(0.35).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.35)^{x-1}(0.35) \\  & =(0.65)^{x-1}(0.35)\end{aligned}
$$

To compute $P(X \gt 3),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X \gt 3) = 1 - P(X \leq  3)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =P(X\in {1,2,3}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & =(0.65)^{1-1}(0.35)+(0.65)^{2-1}(0.35)+(0.65)^{3-1}(0.35) \\  & =(0.35)+(0.65)(0.35)+(0.65)^{2}(0.35) \\  & =[1+0.65+(0.65)^{2}](0.35) \\  & ≈0.725\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, the probability that an applicant who meets all the requirements will appear for the first time after the $3$rd interviewee is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>3) & =1-P(X\le 3) \\  & ≈1-0.725 \\  & ≈0.275\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

feedback.problem: A coin is being randomly picked from a jar and put back in until getting a one-dollar coin. The jar holds a $70%$ of one-dollar coins. What is the probability that a one-dollar coin is chosen before the $5$th trial?  Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of choices before choosing a one-dollar coin. Since the chance of choosing a one-dollar coin is $70%,$ the number of choices required to choose a one-dollar coin can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success

$$
p=70%=\frac{70}{100}=0.7.
$$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.7).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.7)^{x-1}(0.7) \\  & =(0.3)^{x-1}(0.7)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability of choosing a one-dollar coin before the $5$th trial is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<5) & =P(X\in {1,2,3,4}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & =(0.3)^{1-1}(0.7)+(0.3)^{2-1}(0.7)+(0.3)^{3-1}(0.7)+(0.3)^{4-1}(0.7) \\  & =(0.7)+(0.3)(0.7)+(0.3)^{2}(0.7)+(0.3)^{3}(0.7) \\  & =[1+0.3+(0.3)^{2}+(0.3)^{3}](0.7) \\  & ≈0.992\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
